outlier.evidence: Ratings 6/5/5/4 sit within one point of the 5.0 mean. The only rating above threshold, Reviewer_kkfK's 6 at confidence 5, lists the same weaknesses as the 5s and the 4: only Spider, not state of the art, a combination of known techniques.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: One hour spent, confidence 2 ('quite likely that you did not understand central parts'). Limitations field reads 'don't see this section'. Mostly generic praise ('technically sound', 'clearly written'). Its two specific points, the Hard-level loss and the single dataset, are correct (Table 3; Section 4). No discussion comment.

checkable_claims.claim: With large pretrained LMs, the improvement over prior work is within about 1% (Table 2).
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 2, test set: SADGA+BERT-Large 66.7 vs RAT-SQL+BERT-Large 65.6 (+1.1); SADGA+GAP 70.1 vs RAT-SQL+GAP 69.7 (+0.4) and RAT-SQL+GraPPa 69.6 (+0.5). On dev, SADGA+GAP (73.1) is below RAT-SQL+GraPPa (73.4). The authors' 'roughly 2%' reply uses dev-set gains (1.3 to 3.2) against the same-encoder RAT-SQL.

checkable_claims.claim: Without standard errors it is hard to judge whether the improvement is significant.
checkable_claims.evidence: Tables 2-4 give single numbers with no error bars or seed counts. Checklist item 3(c), 'Did you report error bars', answers [Yes]. The authors promised standard errors 'in the future'.

checkable_claims.claim: Lines 38-39, which say existing methods encode the question sequentially and only the schema as a graph, are wrong: since RAT-SQL, SOTA methods encode question and schema jointly.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 38-40 make that claim. The paper's own related work (lines 267-268) says RAT-SQL 'proposes a unified encoding mechanism to improve the joint representation of question and schema'. The authors conceded: 'the presentation is not updated'.

checkable_claims.claim: Experiments are only on Spider, with no results on ATIS, GeoQuery or Advising, and the method is 3rd, not SOTA.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 4 (lines 167-168) evaluates on Spider only. Lines 207-208 and 296-297 report 3rd place on the leaderboard.

checkable_claims.claim: Removing the aggregation component costs only about 2.4%, so other components matter more.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 4, dev set: 'w/o Aggregation' costs 1.8 points for raw SADGA and 2.5 for SADGA+BERT-base. No ablation removes the RAT layers or the tree decoder; the authors confirmed they had not run SADGA-only or RAT-only variants.

checkable_claims.claim: SADGA wins on Extra Hard but is outperformed on Hard in some cases.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 3, test: Hard 57.0 vs RAT-SQL 58.3; Extra Hard 41.7 vs 38.4. Dev: Medium 72.4 vs 73.6.

checkable_claims.claim: Spider contains other datasets (ATIS, GeoQuery, Advising) only in its training part, not in evaluation, so Spider results do not show results on those datasets.
checkable_claims.evidence: Checked against the Spider paper (Yu et al. 2018, 'Data Splits'): it adds 1,659 questions from six older datasets (Restaurants, GeoQuery, Scholar, Academic, IMDB, Yelp) to the training set only. ATIS and Advising are not in Spider at all; WikiSQL supplied tables for about 90 databases, not its questions. So the AC's conclusion holds and its list even overstates Spider's coverage. The submission's lines 170-172 ('contains 9 traditional specific-domain datasets, such as ATIS, GeoQuery, WikiSQL') and the rebuttal ('all these mentioned datasets are subsets of Spider') are false; nine is the number of datasets Spider's Table 1 compares against. The camera-ready keeps the sentence.

rebuttal.evidence: No A review was edited after posting. The public thread holds only the four author responses of 2021-08-10; no reviewer replied in public. The meta-review says the reviewers 'discussed the paper and converged not to support the acceptance'.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: Nothing moved. The defence of Spider-only evaluation rested on a false premise, that ATIS, Advising and WikiSQL are subsets of Spider; the AC answered that the older datasets sit only in Spider's training split. On significance the authors cited dev-set gains of 'roughly 2%' and two test submissions, and promised standard errors 'in the future'. They ran none of the requested experiments: SADGA-only or RAT-only layers and a sequence decoder (Reviewer_kkfK), and the 2-hop masked RAT baseline (Reviewer_QG5a, answered with a description of the pipeline).

ac.evidence: Mean 5.0, three of four below threshold. Both reasons in the meta-review come from the reviews: unclear significance over existing work (Reviewer_QG5a, Reviewer_FKN7) and generalization beyond Spider (Reviewer_kkfK, Reviewer_FKN7, Reviewer_QG5a). The AC's dataset list 'ATIS, GeoQuery, Advising' is kkfK's. The AC attributes the training-split point to the reviewers' discussion and adds its own note that ATIS and GeoQuery queries are harder than Spider's in some respects.

main_reasons_for_decision: Evaluation on Spider only; no evidence that results carry to other text-to-SQL datasets (Reviewer_kkfK, Reviewer_FKN7, Reviewer_QG5a, AC)
Test-set gains over RAT-SQL with large pretrained encoders are about one point, with no error bars (Reviewer_QG5a; AC: 'not clear whether ... significantly better')
Limited reusable insight: known GNN and RAT components recombined for one task (Reviewer_kkfK, Reviewer_va3j, Reviewer_QG5a)
The rebuttal's claim that Spider contains the other datasets was rejected, and no score moved (AC)

outlier.evidence: Ratings 7/7/6/6, mean 6.5; no score departs from the rest. Reviewer_hu28 was at 5 before the rebuttal. Reviewer_RQfk's 7 is uncritical (no weaknesses listed, limitations field 'Yes.') but not out of line with the panel.

checkable_claims.claim: SADGA without external pre-training outperforms the other core models (RAT-SQL, IRNet).
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 2, dev only: SADGA 64.7 vs RAT-SQL 62.7 and IRNet v2 55.4. SADGA has no test number ('blank for the community submission limitation', lines 199-200). Both rows use GloVe, a pretrained vector (lines 178-179), so the comparison is like for like.

checkable_claims.claim: The results show a marked improvement on Spider.
checkable_claims.evidence: Test-set gains over the same-encoder RAT-SQL are 1.1 (BERT-Large) and 0.4 (GAP) points, with no error bars (Table 2). On dev, SADGA+GAP is below RAT-SQL+GraPPa (73.1 vs 73.4). Only dev-set gains with GloVe and BERT-base (2.0 and 3.2) could be called marked, and those have no test numbers.

checkable_claims.claim: The model achieves substantially improved results on the Spider benchmark.
checkable_claims.evidence: Same numbers as for Reviewer_RQfk: test gains of 1.1 and 0.4 points over RAT-SQL with the same pretrained encoder, no error bars.

checkable_claims.claim: In Table 3, SADGA outperforms the baseline more on the two most difficult levels.
checkable_claims.evidence: Holds on dev only (Hard +1.7, Extra Hard +6.5). On test SADGA loses on Hard (57.0 vs 58.3) and wins on Extra Hard (+3.3).

checkable_claims.claim: The authors are upfront that the structure-aware modules reduce accuracy on Easy queries, and SADGA+BERT does not show this trade-off.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 4: removing Local Graph Linking or Aggregation raises Easy accuracy by 1.2 for raw SADGA, but changes it by -0.4 and 0 with BERT-base. Lines 233-238 discuss the Easy-level effect.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper does not say how many parameters SADGA adds over RAT-SQL.
checkable_claims.evidence: No parameter count appears in the submission. The authors' 13M vs 15M figure appears only in the rebuttal.

checkable_claims.claim: The Dual-Graph Encoding (lines 121-125) is very hard to follow; it is unclear how the two graphs and cross-graph edges are combined.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 121-125 are three sentences. They say propagation runs 'among their self-structure' and that relations are represented as nodes. They do not say that no edges cross the two graphs; the authors explained this, and what 'self-structure' means, only in the rebuttal.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_hu28's review, edited 2021-08-15, ends '=== AFTER REBUTTAL I have increased my score (5 --> 6)'; the same-day comment says 'I will increase my score accordingly.' Reviewer_1Eab (2021-08-25) keeps 7, Reviewer_Db2V (2021-08-25) keeps 6, Reviewer_RQfk (2021-09-02) 'My score remains at 7.' RQfk's edit of 2021-07-20 predates the 2021-08-10 rebuttal.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: hu28 was moved by clarifications (graphs encoded separately with relation nodes and no cross-graph edges; deterministic graph construction; fine-tuned pretrained embeddings as node initialisation) and by promises to revise. No new experiment came: the requested BERT-Large and GAP ablation rows were declined for lack of resources. The final review still says the presentation is why 'the paper is not ready yet for publication'. Reviewer_Db2V accepted 13M vs 15M parameters as a controlled comparison.

ac.evidence: All four ratings at 6 or 7. The meta-review opens 'Reviewers are positive about this paper', repeats Reviewer_hu28's raw-model comparison (true on dev only; Table 2 has no test number for raw SADGA), calls performance 'strong', and treats the criticisms as clarity issues that 'can be easily addressed'. It answers hu28's novelty doubt only with 'considered novel and promising', although hu28 called the aggregation itself 'standard gadgets'. It does not mention Reviewer_Db2V's controlled-experiment request. It counts generality as a strength ('can possibly inform and be extended to other tasks') without evidence beyond text-to-SQL.

main_reasons_for_decision: Strong Spider results: 3rd on the leaderboard and dev-set gains over RAT-SQL at every encoder size (Reviewer_1Eab, Reviewer_RQfk, Reviewer_Db2V, Reviewer_hu28)
Aligning question and schema graphs judged novel and promising (Reviewer_1Eab, Reviewer_RQfk, AC)
Raw SADGA beats raw RAT-SQL and IRNet without large pretrained models (Reviewer_hu28, AC)
Criticisms treated as clarity issues fixable in the camera-ready; the rebuttal moved Reviewer_hu28 from 5 to 6

issues_only_a: Evaluation on Spider only; results on ATIS, GeoQuery, Advising or WikiSQL requested (Reviewer_kkfK, Reviewer_FKN7, Reviewer_QG5a, AC). B's Reviewer_1Eab accepted Spider as 'the standard benchmark'
Test margins of about one point may be within RAT-SQL's reported ±0.8-1 training variance; no standard errors (Reviewer_QG5a)
Lines 38-39 misdescribe existing encoders, which have jointly encoded question and schema since RAT-SQL (Reviewer_QG5a)
Not state of the art: 3rd on the leaderboard (Reviewer_kkfK, Reviewer_FKN7, Reviewer_QG5a)
Insight confined to one NLP task, weak fit for NeurIPS; concurrent LGESQL not discussed (Reviewer_QG5a, Reviewer_kkfK)
issues_only_b: Method not described well enough to reproduce: dual-graph encoding (lines 121-125), equation structure, how pretrained embeddings are used (Reviewer_hu28)
No evidence that SADGA helps cross-domain transfer specifically, beyond higher scores (Reviewer_1Eab)
Question graph may lose word order (Reviewer_1Eab)
Related work on unifying text with knowledge bases or code through graphs (Reviewer_Db2V)
shared_issues: Limited novelty: known components recombined (A: Reviewer_kkfK, Reviewer_va3j, Reviewer_QG5a; B: Reviewer_hu28)
Clarity: undefined terms ('undetectable'/'latent association', '1-order word distance'), Figure 1, proofreading (A: Reviewer_va3j, Reviewer_QG5a; B: Reviewer_hu28, Reviewer_Db2V, Reviewer_1Eab)

Whether gains come from SADGA or from extra capacity: A asked for SADGA-only/RAT-only ablations and a 2-hop masked RAT baseline (Reviewer_kkfK, Reviewer_QG5a) and got no experiment; B asked for a parameter-matched control (Reviewer_Db2V) and accepted a parameter count
Uneven results across difficulty levels in Tables 3-4 (A: Reviewer_FKN7; B: Reviewer_RQfk, Reviewer_1Eab)
verdict: The committees weighted the same facts differently, and A's reviewers probed the results harder. Both saw a new encoder module tested only on Spider, a 3rd-place leaderboard result, and an architecture built from known parts. Committee A judged the gains unproven. Reviewer_QG5a said the gain over RAT-SQL with large pretrained encoders is within about one point and has no standard errors; Table 2 confirms test gains of 1.1 (BERT-Large) and 0.4 (GAP), and no table has error bars although checklist item 3(c) answers [Yes]. Three of four A reviewers asked for other datasets. The authors replied that ATIS, Advising and WikiSQL 'are subsets of Spider'. That is false: Spider adds questions from six older datasets, and only to its training split. A's AC, citing the reviewers' discussion, made the training-split point and rejected. Committee B never raised the single-benchmark or variance questions. Two of its reviewers called the gains 'marked' and 'substantially improved', which the test numbers do not support, and its criticisms were mainly about clarity. The rebuttal promised fixes, and Reviewer_hu28 moved from 5 to 6 with no new experiment. A's panel also had more text-to-SQL depth (Reviewer_kkfK at confidence 5; QG5a on RAT-SQL's training variance and LGESQL), while B's Reviewer_1Eab calls itself 'a reader without too much experience on the Spider dataset'. Whether Spider-only evaluation disqualifies a NeurIPS paper is a judgment call, but A's factual claims hold and B overstated the margins.
